records.name: Applied Mechanics
records.summary: A Philadelphia theater company that makes immersive plays about social change. Its current show, a satire called Run Ben Run, runs October 6 to 18, 2026.
records.what_you_do: Performers and a director build original plays for live audiences. You can buy tickets to a show, or sign up for the mailing list to hear about new productions.

schedule.text: Run Ben Run plays October 6 to 18, 2026 at Christ Church Neighborhood House. Showtimes are not on the home page.

locations.label: Christ Church Neighborhood House (venue for Run Ben Run)

cost.text: Ticket prices are not shown on the home page.

first_step.how: Buy tickets to Run Ben Run through the Ticketleap link on the home page, or sign up for the mailing list on the contact page
first_step.basis: Shows are open to the public and buying a ticket is the clear first step, but the page does not say how to join the company itself.

records.notes: Legal form is not stated, so kind is program. The page names grant funders, which suggests a nonprofit, but that is not confirmed. Category and tag are the closest fits for a theater company. The mailing list sign-up is on the contact page, which was not read.

records.name: Asian Mosaic Fund
records.notes: A giving circle that pools member donations and makes grants to Asian American and Pacific Islander community organizations. The site does not say whether it is a private foundation, but it works as a grantmaker, and its main public actions are donating and applying for grants. Hidden under the grantmaker rule. Re-check if the site later shows a member program people can join.

records.name: Beyond the Bell Tours
records.notes: A guided walking tour business that sells tours through a booking platform. The site describes itself as a social enterprise, which makes it a business, so it is not listed as a group. No dated events.

records.name: Center City Jazz Festival
records.notes: A one-time annual jazz festival held at several Center City venues. The newest dated item is April 22, 2023 (ninth annual). No ongoing programs or meetings are shown, so it is not a group. The page names no phone or email, and the ticket link shows no prices.

records.name: CultureBanq
records.notes: An arts funding and investment network working across the United States. The site does not state its legal form, and it lists no community program that a visitor could join. Its only public actions are donating and a newsletter form, which the page says is not yet working. The dated items are years of cited reports (2023 to 2025), not events. Hidden under the funder rule.

records.name: First Degree Consulting
records.notes: A consulting business that advises local governments, nonprofits, universities and philanthropic groups. It has no community program that a member of the public can join. No dated events.

records.name: Glitter
records.notes: A benefit corporation that sells a paid block litter cleanup service. Residents pledge money on their block page, and the pooled money pays for weekly cleanups. It is a business, so it is not listed as a group. The site also offers paid cleaner jobs. No dated items are shown.

records.name: Philadelphia Center for Gun Violence Reporting
records.summary: Researchers, journalists and gun violence survivors working to make news coverage of gun violence more accurate and fair. The group publishes studies and reporting guides, keeps a directory of survivors who will speak to the press, and hosts events.
records.what_you_do: Read the free reporting guides and research, sign up for the newsletter, and attend events the group hosts. Journalists can use the survivor directory.

schedule.text: Events are announced on the site and in the newsletter. No regular schedule is published.

cost.text: Public resources and the newsletter are free. The site also takes optional donations.

first_step.how: Sign up for the newsletter on the site, or read the public reporting resources
first_step.basis: Public resources and a newsletter are open to all, but the page does not describe volunteering, membership or meetings, so the way in is unclear.

records.notes: The lead called it the Initiative for Better Gun Violence Reporting. The site calls the group PCGVR and gives the IBGVR name in its CultureWorks mailing address, so both names refer to one group. No email or phone is on the home page, and the contact page was not read. The site does not say whether it is nonpartisan. It reads as a research and reporting project, not a political group.

records.name: Inti Media
records.summary: A media organization that makes news, films and podcasts with a focus on Black and Latin American communities. Its news sections are in English, Spanish and Portuguese, and community members can pitch story ideas.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer to help with stories, pitch a story idea, attend a seasonal community pitch meeting, or sign up for the monthly newsletter.

schedule.text: Community pitch meetings are held seasonally and linked from the events page. Dates are not shown on the page.

cost.text: No fees are listed for volunteering, pitch meetings or the newsletter. Donations are optional.

first_step.how: Email production@intimedia.org to offer help or pitch a story, or sign up for the monthly newsletter
first_step.basis: The page names volunteering and open community pitch meetings as ways in, and gives an email address.

records.notes: Legal form is not stated. Donations go through a fiscal sponsor, which suggests a nonprofit project, but that is not confirmed, so kind is program. The only 2026 item is a fellow title on the team page, which is not an event, so status is probably_active rather than active. The site places the group in Philadelphia. The community focus comes from the site's own statement. The mailing address for checks is at CultureWorks Greater Philadelphia and is not a public office, so it is not listed as a location.

records.name: Outsiders Improvised & Creative Music Festival
records.notes: An annual festival series organized by Jam-All Productions, per the artist's site. Editions run from 2015 to 2023, and the newest Philadelphia items are a November and December 2022 festival and a June 2023 pop-up. The series is an event, not a group, so it is not listed. The site also names Masterclass Workshops and Tour Ready Projects, which were not read. They could be a separate future lead.

records.name: Sotomayor Productions
records.notes: A one-person production company presented under the filmmaker's own name, with booking, screening and donation links. It is not a group that people join. The page shows no dated items, and years in its link addresses were not treated as dates.

records.name: Spiral Q
records.summary: A Philadelphia-area arts group that uses public art and community projects to bring people, neighborhoods and causes together. It works through the year with students, neighbors and activists.
records.what_you_do: Join the mailing list, contact the group to ask about projects or volunteering, or support the work with donations or supplies.

schedule.text: No schedule is published. The site names a project called Peoplehood 2026, with no month shown.

first_step.how: Email community@spiralq.org or call 215-222-6979 to ask how to take part, or sign up for the mailing list on the site
first_step.basis: The site invites students, neighbors and activists to get involved, but it describes no public events or hours, so the way in is unclear.

records.notes: The lead called it Spiral Q LLC. The site does not state its legal form, so it is listed as Spiral Q and kind is program. Its jobs and work-with-us pages were not read. The site names Peoplehood 2026 with no month, so there is no dated event. Whether the public can attend anything is not stated, so check before showing it as walk-in.

records.name: The Stained Glass Project
records.summary: A nonprofit that teaches stained glass classes and one-day workshops in Philadelphia. Workshop fees help fund free programming for Philadelphia public high school students.
records.what_you_do: Take a one-day stained glass workshop and make a small piece from a pre-designed pattern, such as a sun catcher or ornament. No experience is needed for most workshops.

schedule.text: Multi-week classes and one-day workshops are listed on the classes page. The page shows no dates or times, and each class has its own listing page.

cost.text: The one-day workshops listed on the classes page are $150 each.

first_step.how: Pick a class on the classes page and sign up through its listing, or email windowsthatopendoors@gmail.com with questions (the group says replies take 24 to 48 hours)
first_step.basis: The page says no experience is needed for most workshops and that most suit beginners, and it gives an email address for questions.

records.notes: The lead called it The Stained Glass Project. The site calls itself Windows That Open Doors and uses both names, so one record covers both. Stained glass is not a listed tag, so craft_circle is the closest fit. The class listings have no dates. Image file names suggest 2026, but the page does not state it, so no date is recorded. Individual class listing pages were not read.

records.name: Tiny Farm Wagon
records.summary: A mobile art project that builds gardens, runs workshops and holds art events. It works as an art classroom, greenhouse and gallery on wheels, and it cooks plant-based food in a cob oven.
records.what_you_do: Take part in workshops and art events, help build the gardens, or email the project to ask about programs.

schedule.text: No schedule or dates are published on the page.

first_step.how: Email tinyfarmwagon@gmail.com for information about programs
first_step.basis: The project invites inquiries about programs, but the page gives no schedule, sign-up steps or cost, so the way in is unclear.

records.notes: The page is a project page on an artist's site. It names CultureTrust of Greater Philadelphia but does not state the project's legal form, so kind is program. No dates or location are on the page. The page invites visitors to subscribe for news, but gives no sign-up link.

records.name: Trash Academy
records.summary: A campaign against litter and illegal dumping in Philadelphia. It asks the city to adopt the Clean Philadelphia NOW platform, and it is backed by a coalition of groups and individuals.
records.what_you_do: Sign on to the Clean Philadelphia NOW platform, join the coalition, or watch the recorded planning sessions and campaign resources on litter and dumping.

schedule.text: Planning sessions are listed by weekday and month only, with no year shown. No regular meeting schedule is published.

cost.text: Signing the platform is free. The site also accepts donations.

first_step.how: Sign on to the Clean Philadelphia NOW platform from the campaign page, or email trashacademy@muralarts.org to join the coalition
first_step.basis: Anyone can sign on or email to join, with no application or dues mentioned.

records.notes: Sessions are listed with weekdays and months but no year. The weekdays and dates line up with 2022 calendar dates, but the page does not state a year, so no year is recorded and status stays unknown. The contact email is on the muralarts.org domain, which the page does not explain. No petition link or mailing address is published. The site also lists a Happening now label, which has no dates behind it.

records.name: We3 Gardens
records.summary: A neighborhood garden project that creates shared spaces for growing, learning and gathering in the city. It started with raised beds, flowers, herbs and places to sit.
records.what_you_do: Come see what is growing, help with the garden (the page says no green thumb is needed), or contact the team to support the projects.

schedule.text: No hours or work-day schedule is published on the page.

first_step.how: Visit the project page on The Homesteadista site and use its contact details to ask about visiting or helping
first_step.basis: The page invites visitors and says no green thumb is needed, but it gives no hours or sign-up steps, so the way in is unclear.

records.notes: The lead called it We Three Gardens. The site spells it We3 Gardens. The Homesteadista is a small brand that offers workshops and consulting, so it is not listed as a group, but its We3 Gardens project is. The page names CultureTrust Greater Philadelphia as a fiscal sponsor. The only date is in the web address of a mini-grant link, which is not page text, so it is not used. The support email on the page belongs to a named person, so it is left out of the record. Location and hours are not published.

records.name: West Philly Bizarre
records.summary: A nonprofit maker market where vendors can sell for little or no cost. It runs a seasonal market at Clark Park, pop-up shops and workshops during the year.
records.what_you_do: Shop at the Clark Park market on select Saturdays, visit a pop-up, take a workshop, or apply to sell at a future market (vendor applications are closed right now).

schedule.text: The Clark Park market runs on select Saturdays from April through November. The site lists a pop-up shop from April 1 to June 7 and a May 31 workshop, with no year shown.

locations.label: Bizarre at Clark Park (street address not on the page)

cost.text: Visitor cost is not stated. The site lists a $45 nail workshop and a $15 donation that pays for one vendor table at Clark Park.

first_step.how: Visit the Clark Park market on a Saturday from April to November, or sign up for the newsletter on the site
first_step.basis: Markets are open to the public. Vendor spots are applied for, and applications are closed on the page right now.

records.notes: The site gives event dates without a year, and its copyright line is not used as evidence, so no last_sign_of_life is set. The Clark Park street address is not on the page. The only street address on the page is the pop-up at 3610 Lancaster Ave. Vendor fees are listed; visitor cost is not. The site says vendor applications usually open in late winter.

records.name: You'll Never Forget Productions
records.notes: A media production company that makes history documentaries and podcasts, and takes on projects for organizations. It is a business, so it is not listed as a group. The page lists no shows, events, prices or email address.

records.name: Working Writers Group
records.summary: A group of Philadelphia-area authors who meet to talk through each other's work. It has met monthly since 1985 and is the parent group behind the New Door Books literary press.
records.what_you_do: Attend the monthly meeting to discuss each other's writing with other authors.

schedule.text: Meets monthly. The page does not give a day, time or meeting place.

first_step.how: Call New Door Books at 215-769-2525 and ask how to get in touch with the group, since the page does not say how to join
first_step.basis: The group has met for decades, but the page does not say whether it takes new writers or how to join.

records.notes: No own website was found. The group is described on the About page of New Door Books, the literary press that the page calls a project of the group. The phone number is the press's, not a group line. The press's address is not used as a meeting place. Status is unknown: the page says the group has met monthly since 1985, in the present tense, but the only dated items are 1985 and 2009.

records.name: Bella Vista Neighbors Association
records.summary: The all-volunteer neighborhood group for Bella Vista, a registered community organization since 1992. It runs neighborhood street sweeping, works with police on safety, takes part in zoning and historic preservation, and sends out neighborhood alerts.
records.what_you_do: Sweep your block with the group, attend announced meetings, join a committee, or sign up for the mailing list.

schedule.text: The page says the group holds monthly PSA1 meetings but gives no dates, times or place. Meetings are announced when scheduled.

locations.label: Bella Vista (the group's land use area runs from South to Washington, 6th to 11th streets)

cost.text: No cost is listed for joining, volunteering or the mailing list. Donations are accepted.

first_step.how: Email info@bellavistaneighbors.org to join, sign up for the mailing list on the site, or sweep your block with the group
first_step.basis: The site invites neighbors to email to join and to attend announced meetings. No application or dues are mentioned.

records.notes: The lead named it Bella Vista Neighborhood Association from the Our Market Project page, which names it without a link. The group's own site spells it Bella Vista Neighbors Association and abbreviates it BVNA. Treated as the same group, since both describe the Bella Vista neighborhood association. A 2017 Passyunk Post article reported the group might dissolve after losing insurance. Its outcome was not found, and the site presents the group as active. The site has no dated events. Its mailing address is a PO Box, not a meeting place. Leadership names are not on the site.

leads_only.note: Trash Academy's contact email uses this domain. Not checked.

leads_only.name: Every Voice Every Vote
leads_only.note: Named in a PCGVR news item as the host of a Philadelphia community panel. Not checked.

leads_only.name: Painted Bride Art Center
leads_only.note: Venue for 2022 Outsiders festival events, listed with an address only. Not checked.

leads_only.name: Village of Industry & Art
leads_only.note: The building at 320 S Broad St where The Stained Glass Project holds its classes. Not checked.

leads_only.name: Fiera Studios
leads_only.note: Named as the lead of Our Market Project, a public art and oral history project at the Italian Market. Not checked.

notes: Lane M, 24 leads. Records: 11 publish, 2 hide (both out_of_scope), 7 not_a_group. Not recorded: Root Quarterly and Till Arts Project (empty pages on two tries, listed in blocked), Community Unity Music Festival (domain does not resolve, listed in blocked), and Moonstone Arts Center (only a submission page is linked and the single WebSearch was used on Bella Vista, so it is skipped and not put in leads_only). Searches used: 1 of 1. Fetches used: 32. No rate limiting seen beyond the empty pages and one DNS error. Low-confidence publish records: Spiral Q, Tiny Farm Wagon, We3 Gardens, Working Writers Group (no own site). Trash Academy status is unknown because its sessions have no year shown. Undated items were given no year.
